newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU suspends work on clearer job-quotas law.
newsitem.headline: EU suspends work on clearer job-quotas law.

text.p: The Social Affairs Council on Thursday shelved indefinitely a proposal to clarify EU law on job quotas for women.
"There was no need for the proposals ever to have been submitted," Dutch Employment Minister Ad Melkert told a news conference in Luxembourg.

The ministers were debating a European Commission text aimed at clarifying a 1995 European Court of Justice ruling that struck down a German quota scheme because it gave women "absolute and conditional" priority for some jobs and promotions.
The Commission wants to ensure that other "positive action" programmes to boost women's job prospects women are deemed legal under EU law.
"I'm disappointed that they (the ministers) are not going ahead with it right now," EU Social Affairs Commissioner Padraig Flynn said.
He said the EU executive believed it was critical to encourage equal opportunities and that EU law had to be absolutely clear about which measures were legal and which were not.
The Commission argues that the so-called Kalanke judgment, which said the German quota scheme violated a 1976 EU equal opportunities directive, 76/207/EEC, should be interpreted narrowly.
Its text would assure employers they could adopt plans to boost the number of women who are hired or promoted as long as they did not turn into rigid quotas.

Melkert, whose country holds the EU presidency, acknowledged that clarifications were needed but said EU governments wanted to wait for the outcome of their talks over EU treaty reforms, which will not be completed until June.
They are considering proposals to expand the scope of provisions on equal opportunities for men and women.
Melkert said ministers also wanted to wait and see how case law on job quotas developed.
